html:
The Kaxarari are a small Panoan-speaking people of the western Amazon, on the borders of the states of Rondônia, Acre and Amazonas in Brazil. Their language is the most divergent of the main Panoan branch, distantly related to those of the Huni Kuin and Shipibo.

Like many peoples of the region, they lost land and lives to rubber tappers during the rubber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s, and later to logging and ranching. They now hold a recognised Indigenous territory in Brazil, where a few hundred people live.
